Our Mission

We started this because we believe no one should feel forgotten. Our mission is to show up for seniors, veterans, and families who are homebound — whether that's because of a lack of transportation, a medical condition, or a financial barrier — along with any family in our community facing hard times. No one should feel abandoned, forgotten, or face hunger alone. Every box we pack, we pack with care, because behind every person we serve is a story, a name, and a life we genuinely want to look after. You are seen. You are loved. And you don't have to carry this alone. Right now we're proud to serve Mesa, with a goal to grow and reach families across all of Maricopa County.

Our Story

Because no one should have to carry this alone.

An elderly man on the side of the road, pulling a small wagon behind his bicycle, making the long trip to the grocery store because it was the only way he had. No car. No ride. Just him, the Arizona heat pressing down on his shoulders, and a wagon that could barely hold what he needed to get through the week. It's the kind of sight that stops you mid-step — one you can't quite forget once you've seen it.

Imagine how tired he must have been. How long that ride must have felt under that sun. How easy it would have been for someone to simply carry those groceries to his door instead. And once you really see one neighbor like that, you start seeing all the others — the parents quietly stretching too little too far, the veterans who'd rather go without than ask for help, the seniors who just want someone, anyone, to remember they exist. Once something like that breaks open in you, it doesn't close back up.

So groceries were packed and driven straight to his door. The look on his face when it opened — surprise, then something softer, something like relief. That one small act is the whole reason Bread & Blessings exists. There was no grand plan behind it, just tears in a driveway and a decision that no one in our community should have to carry that much alone. We've grown since then, but the heart of it hasn't changed one bit — we still show up the way we did that very first day: in person, and we show up with compassion.

This is a labor of love, plain and simple — built entirely by volunteers who give up their evenings and weekends, and neighbors who give what little extra they have, so that every dollar and every bag of groceries lands exactly where it's needed most. If you're struggling right now, please, let us carry a little of that weight with you — you don't have to hold it alone. And if you're able to give, know that your kindness won't just sit in a warehouse somewhere. It will end up in someone's arms, on someone's doorstep, at the exact moment they needed to know they haven't been forgotten.

What guides us

  • We show up for people exactly as they are, and love them through whatever they're carrying
  • This is family taking care of family — Mesa neighbors showing up for Mesa neighbors
  • We grow slowly and sustainably, one relationship at a time
  • Every gift you give goes straight into a neighbor's hands
Programs

How we care for our neighbors

Whatever the need, our approach stays the same: meet people with warmth, and get them what they need without delay.

Monthly Food Boxes

Packed pantry and fresh-item boxes delivered directly to families' doors, once a month, every month.

Neighbor Referrals

Community members, schools, and churches can flag a family who could use a hand — we reach out ourselves, gently and with an open heart.

Donation Drives

Seasonal drives for shelf-stable food and gift cards that keep our shelves — and our families' pantries — stocked.

Get Help

You don't have to go without.

Reach out, and one of our volunteers will personally follow up within a few days — with care and a listening ear.

Donate

Your generosity becomes the reason someone is not left hungry or forgotten.

Food, gift cards, or a one-time gift — every bit goes straight to a Mesa family who needed to be reminded they're not alone. We're a registered 501(c)(3), so your gift is tax-deductible, but the real return is a full table and a lighter heart.
